description: Whole sea bass fillets, their skin scored and crisped over hot coals, served alongside a vivid, herb-thunderous salsa verde of capers, anchovies, and every green herb you can find — Mediterranean summer on a plate, light as a breeze and full of forward, punchy flavour. The salsa verde does more than sauce the fish: it pulls together the entire dish with its bright, briny intensity. Ready in under half an hour.
kidNote: For children who are less keen on strong flavours, serve the salsa verde on the side rather than spooned over the fish, and offer a simple squeeze of lemon instead.
ingredients: 4 sea bass fillets (about 180g each), skin on, scaled
steps: Make the salsa verde: finely chop the parsley, basil, and mint together. Finely chop the anchovies and capers. Combine all herbs, anchovies, capers, garlic (minced), mustard, olive oil, and vinegar. Stir well, taste, and adjust the seasoning.
Score the skin of each sea bass fillet 3 times diagonally with a sharp knife, cutting just through the skin. Pat dry with kitchen paper.
Brush both sides of each fillet with olive oil and season well. Ensure the BBQ grate is very clean and very hot — brush with oil immediately before cooking.

Place the fillets skin-side down on the hot grate. Cook without moving for 4-5 minutes until the skin is deeply golden and the flesh has turned opaque two-thirds of the way up. Flip carefully and cook for a further 1-2 minutes.
Transfer to warm plates, spoon the salsa verde generously over each fillet, and serve immediately with lemon wedges.
tip: A very clean, very hot, well-oiled grate is essential for fish — any residue causes sticking. Heat the grate for at least 10 minutes before cooking, then brush with a folded paper towel dipped in oil.

name: Chargrilled Lamb Chops with Herbed Yoghurt
description: Thick-cut lamb loin chops marinated in rosemary, garlic, and lemon, grilled over fierce coals until charred at the edges and rosy-pink within — lamb this way smells extraordinary as it hits the heat, releasing a perfume of fat and herb that drifts across any garden. The herbed yoghurt, cool and sharp with garlic and mint, is the ideal counterpoint to the richness of the meat.
kidNote: Lamb chops can be a little rich for young children — offer smaller pieces off the bone with the yoghurt sauce as a dipping accompaniment.
ingredients: 2 sprigs fresh rosemary, leaves finely chopped
small bunch of mint, finely chopped
steps: Combine the olive oil, garlic, rosemary, lemon zest and juice, and cumin to make the marinade. Coat the lamb chops thoroughly, season well, and leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature.
Make the herbed yoghurt: mix the Greek yoghurt with the garlic, mint, lemon juice, and salt. Refrigerate until needed.
Heat the barbecue to high. Allow the chops to come to room temperature if marinated in the fridge.
Grill the chops over direct high heat for 3-4 minutes per side for medium — pink and juicy within, with a charred, fragrant crust. Rest on a warm plate for 5 minutes.
Serve the chops on a platter with the herbed yoghurt alongside, fresh flatbreads, and a simple tomato and cucumber salad.
tip: Let the chops come fully to room temperature before grilling — cold meat from the fridge lowers the grate temperature and prevents proper searing, resulting in steamed rather than charred lamb.

name: Chermoula Prawn Skewers with Flatbread
description: Fat king prawns threaded onto skewers and marinated in chermoula — a Moroccan herb and spice paste of coriander, cumin, smoked paprika, and preserved lemon — then grilled over hot coals until the shells char and the flesh turns sweet and smoky. The chermoula does double duty as marinade and sauce: half goes on the raw prawns, half is stirred through at the end as a dressing.
kidNote: Children who enjoy prawns usually love these — reduce the chilli in the chermoula and the flavour is aromatic rather than spicy. Peel the prawns before threading for easier eating.
ingredients: flatbreads and lemon wedges, to serve
steps: Make the chermoula: blitz the coriander, garlic, cumin, paprika, chilli, preserved lemon skin, lemon juice, and olive oil in a food processor until you have a rough, bright-green paste. Season with salt.
Toss the prawns with half the chermoula in a bowl, ensuring every prawn is well coated. Leave to marinate for 15-30 minutes.
Thread 4-5 prawns onto each skewer, threading through both the head and tail end to keep them from spinning when turned.
Grill over high direct heat for 2-3 minutes per side until the shells are charred and the flesh is opaque all the way through. Don't overcook — prawns tighten and toughen rapidly.
Transfer to a warm platter, spoon over the reserved chermoula, and serve with warm flatbreads and lemon wedges.
tip: Shell-on prawns protect the flesh from the fierce heat and add flavour as the shells char — peel them at the table for maximum taste.

name: Grilled Halloumi Skewers with Harissa & Pomegranate
description: Thick cubes of halloumi, golden and yielding from the grill, interspersed with sweet red peppers and courgette on skewers, finished with a smear of rose harissa and a jewel-scatter of pomegranate seeds — a vegetarian BBQ main that nobody feels short-changed by. The halloumi takes on a gorgeous char from the grill while remaining pillowy inside, and the harissa brings a fragrant, complex heat.
kidNote: Most children love grilled halloumi for its mild, salty flavour and springy texture — serve their skewers with just a little mild yoghurt dip and skip the harissa.
ingredients: 2 x 225g blocks halloumi, cut into 2.5cm cubes
2 red peppers, deseeded and cut into 3cm chunks
small bunch of fresh mint, leaves torn
steps: Thread the halloumi, red pepper, and courgette alternately onto skewers. Brush generously all over with olive oil and season with black pepper.
Mix the harissa and honey together in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Grill over medium-high direct heat for 3-4 minutes per side until the halloumi is golden with clear char marks and the vegetables have softened and charred at the edges.
In the final minute of cooking, brush the skewers with the harissa-honey glaze and allow it to caramelise briefly.
Transfer to a platter, scatter with pomegranate seeds and fresh mint, and serve with the Greek yoghurt and warm flatbreads alongside.
tip: Don't move the skewers for the first 3 minutes — halloumi needs time to build a crust that releases cleanly from the grate. Moving it too early tears the cheese and causes sticking.

name: Double Smash Burgers with American Cheese & Pickles
description: Loosely packed beef patties smashed hard onto a screaming-hot griddle plate, their edges crisping and lace-like with the Maillard crust that defines a great burger. Two thin patties stacked with melted American cheese, dill pickles, shredded iceberg, and a special sauce in a toasted brioche bun deliver more flavour per mouthful than any thick patty ever could. Fast, messy, and enormously satisfying.
kidNote: Children adore smash burgers — keep it simple with just cheese, ketchup, and a little iceberg for younger guests, and cut in half for easier eating.
steps: Mix together all sauce ingredients (mayonnaise, mustard, ketchup, pickle brine, garlic powder) in a small bowl and refrigerate. Divide the beef mince into 8 loosely packed balls (about 100g each) — don't compact them.
Set a heavy cast-iron griddle plate directly on the BBQ grate over high heat until smoking. Brush lightly with oil.
Place 2 beef balls onto the griddle at a time, spaced apart. Immediately smash each ball flat with a heavy spatula or burger press, pressing firmly for 10 seconds. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook for 2-2.5 minutes until the edges are deeply brown and crispy. Flip, immediately lay a slice of cheese on each patty, and cook for 1 minute more. Stack two cheesy patties together.
Toast the cut sides of the brioche buns on the griddle for 30 seconds. Assemble: sauce on both cut sides, then shredded lettuce, pickles, and the double patty stack. Serve at once.
tip: The key to the smash burger is very high heat and a single, decisive press — you're maximising contact between the meat and the cooking surface. Never press a smash burger twice or move it before the 2-minute crust has formed.

name: Thai Green Vegetable Curry with Jasmine Rice
description: Fragrant coconut milk curry with courgette, aubergine and spinach in a vivid green paste sauce. The trick is adding spinach off the heat so it wilts gently without dulling the colour.
kidNote: Use less curry paste for a milder version — start with 1 tbsp and taste before adding more
tip: Don't simmer the coconut milk for too long once the vegetables are added — it can split. Keep the heat at a gentle bubble.
ingredients: small bunch of basil or coriander
steps: Cook the jasmine rice per packet instructions. Heat the oil in a wok or large deep pan over medium-high heat, add the curry paste and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in half the coconut milk, stir well to loosen the paste, then add the aubergine. Cook for 5 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the remaining coconut milk, courgette and green beans. Simmer for 8–10 minutes until all the vegetables are just tender but still have a little bite.
Season with soy sauce, brown sugar and lime juice. Taste and adjust — it should be creamy, a little spicy, balanced with a hint of sweetness.
Remove from the heat, fold in the spinach and leave for 1 minute to wilt gently. Scatter over fresh basil or coriander and serve with the jasmine rice.

name: Mapo Tofu with Steamed Rice
description: Silken tofu trembling in a deeply savoury, lip-tingling Sichuan sauce of fermented black beans, doubanjiang and chilli oil. One of the most addictive vegetarian dishes in the world.
kidNote: This is genuinely spicy — make a small batch of plain silken tofu with soy sauce and sesame oil for younger children
tip: Doubanjiang (spicy broad bean paste) is the soul of this dish — find it in any Asian supermarket. Without it you'll have a nice tofu dish, but not mapo tofu.
ingredients: 600g silken or soft tofu, cut into 2cm cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, roughly chopped
1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
2 tsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Cook the rice. Gently lower the tofu cubes into a pan of simmering salted water for 3 minutes to firm slightly. Drain carefully.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the doubanjiang and fry for 1 minute until the oil turns red and fragrant. Add the garlic, ginger and black beans, stir-fry for another minute.
Pour in the stock, add the soy sauce and bring to a boil. Carefully slide in the tofu and simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the cornflour slurry and cook for 1–2 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to coat the tofu. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Drizzle with sesame oil, scatter over the ground Sichuan pepper and spring onions. Serve immediately over steamed rice.

name: Korean Vegetable Bibimbap with Gochujang
description: A Korean rice bowl with individually seasoned vegetables and a fried egg, everything brought together with a spoonful of fiery, sticky gochujang sauce. Mix everything at the table.
kidNote: Serve the gochujang sauce on the side — the vegetables and egg over rice are mild and delicious without the heat
tip: Sauté each vegetable separately and season each one individually — this is what gives bibimbap its distinctive character over a simple stir-fry.
steps: Cook the rice. Make the sauce: mix gochujang, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp soy sauce and rice vinegar with 1 tbsp warm water until smooth.
Sauté each vegetable separately in a little oil and garlic, seasoning each with a dash of soy sauce and sesame oil. Keep them separate — the individual preparation is key to bibimbap.
Divide the hot cooked rice into 4 bowls. Arrange the vegetables in sections over the rice, keeping each type distinct.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in the same pan, keeping the yolks runny. Place one egg on top of each bowl.
Drizzle with the gochujang sauce and sesame seeds. Bring to the table and let everyone mix everything together vigorously — the bowl should be stirred to combine all the flavours.

name: Vegetarian Pad Thai
description: Flat rice noodles tangled with egg, crispy tofu, crunchy beansprouts and spring onions, everything coated in a sweet-sour tamarind sauce. Finished with roasted peanuts and lime.
kidNote: Leave out the chilli flakes and they'll love the mild peanut-noodle flavour — serve the lime and peanuts on the side for customising
tip: Work in batches if needed — an overcrowded wok steams instead of fries, and you'll lose the smoky wok flavour that makes pad thai so distinctive.
steps: Soak rice noodles in cold water for 20 minutes then drain. Mix together tamarind paste, soy sauce, brown sugar and lime juice to make the sauce.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over very high heat. Fry the tofu until golden on all sides, about 4 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining oil and fry garlic for 30 seconds. Push to the side, scramble the beaten eggs until just set, then break up and mix through.
Add the drained noodles and sauce. Toss constantly for 2–3 minutes until the noodles absorb the sauce and start to caramelise at the edges.
Return the tofu, add the beansprouts and most of the spring onions, toss for 1 minute. Plate up and top with peanuts, remaining spring onions, chilli flakes and coriander. Serve with lime wedges.

name: Sichuan Aubergine with Garlic & Ginger
description: Silky, almost-melting aubergine in a deeply savoury, garlicky sauce with a Sichuan kick. The aubergine soaks up the glossy sauce completely — this tastes far more complex than it is to make.
kidNote: Reduce or omit the chilli bean paste for a milder, sweeter version that's just as delicious
tip: Salt the aubergine and leave for 15 minutes to draw out moisture — it collapses faster during cooking and absorbs the sauce more readily.
ingredients: 1 tbsp doubanjiang or chilli bean paste
steps: Toss the aubergine with salt and leave in a colander for 15 minutes. Pat dry. Cook the rice.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat until smoking. Fry the aubergine in batches for 5–6 minutes until golden and collapsing. Set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok, fry garlic and ginger for 1 minute. Add the chilli bean paste and cook for another minute until fragrant and the oil turns red.
Return the aubergine to the wok. Add soy sauce, vinegar and sugar, toss to coat everything.
Pour in the cornflour mixture, stir for 1–2 minutes until the sauce thickens and glossily coats the aubergine. Finish with sesame oil and spring onions. Serve over rice.

name: Black Bean & Cheese Enchiladas
description: Corn tortillas rolled around spiced black beans and melted cheese, baked under a blanketing chipotle tomato sauce until bubbling and golden. Proper Mexican comfort food.
kidNote: Use plain passata instead of chipotle and reduce chilli for a milder version that kids will happily eat
tip: Warm the tortillas before rolling — either 30 seconds in a dry pan or wrapped in damp kitchen paper in the microwave. Cold tortillas crack when rolled.
ingredients: soured cream and coriander, to serve
steps: Heat oven to 200°C/180°C fan. Make the sauce: fry the onion in oil for 5 minutes, add garlic for 1 minute, then add tomatoes and chipotle paste. Simmer for 10 minutes until thickened. Season well.
Roughly mash the black beans with a fork, mixing in cumin, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt — leave some beans whole for texture.
Warm the tortillas briefly. Spoon beans down the centre of each, scatter over half the cheese, then roll tightly and pack seam-side down into an ovenproof dish.
Pour the tomato sauce over the top, scatter over the remaining cheese. Bake for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Serve with a generous dollop of soured cream and scattered fresh coriander.

name: Roasted Sweet Potato & Black Bean Tacos
description: Smoky, cumin-roasted sweet potato with black beans piled into warm corn tortillas with avocado, pickled red onion and soured cream. Bright and satisfying with every bite.
kidNote: Kids love the sweet potato filling — serve in smaller tortillas and let them build their own tacos
tip: Cut the sweet potato into even 1cm cubes so they roast evenly — too large and the middles stay hard, too small and they turn to mush.
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
steps: Heat oven to 220°C/200°C fan. Toss sweet potato with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, chilli flakes and salt. Spread on a baking tray and roast for 25 minutes until caramelised at the edges.
Quick-pickle the red onion: toss sliced onion with 2 tbsp lime juice and a pinch of salt. Leave for at least 20 minutes — it will turn bright pink.
Warm the black beans in a pan with a pinch of cumin. Mash the avocado roughly with remaining lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Char the tortillas directly over a gas flame for 30 seconds per side, or in a dry pan, until slightly blistered.
Pile sweet potato and black beans into the tortillas. Top with smashed avocado, pickled onion, soured cream and coriander.

name: Sizzling Veggie Fajitas with Guacamole
description: Charred strips of pepper and onion with smoky spices, brought to the table still sizzling with warm flour tortillas, fresh guacamole and soured cream. A hands-on dinner everyone builds themselves.
kidNote: Let children fill their own tortillas — they're always more excited to eat something they've assembled themselves
tip: Get the pan screaming hot before the vegetables go in — you want charring and colour, not steaming. Cook in batches if needed.
ingredients: 2 large red onions, sliced into wedges
steps: Make guacamole: mash avocados with lime juice, diced red onion, coriander and a pinch of salt. Keep chunky.
Toss the sliced peppers and onion wedges with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano. Season generously.
Heat a large cast iron or heavy frying pan until very hot. Cook the vegetables in batches for 8–10 minutes until charred in spots and softened. Don't stir too often — you want colour.
Warm the tortillas wrapped in foil in a low oven, or briefly in a dry pan.
Bring the sizzling vegetables to the table in the pan along with all the accompaniments — let everyone build their own.

name: Chipotle Bean Burrito Bowl
description: Smoky chipotle black beans and lime-spiked coriander rice, piled with avocado, sweetcorn and soured cream. Faster than queueing at the real thing and genuinely better.
kidNote: Skip the chipotle for a milder bean bowl — the sweetcorn, rice and avocado combination is a universal kids' hit
tip: Season the rice while hot with lime juice and fresh coriander — plain rice under the beans makes the whole bowl feel flat.
steps: Cook the rice. Fluff with a fork and stir through lime juice and chopped coriander while still hot.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin and garlic powder, fry for 30 seconds. Add the tomatoes and chipotle paste, simmer for 5 minutes until thickened.
Add the black beans, stir to coat, simmer for another 5 minutes until the sauce is absorbed and the beans are deeply flavourful. Season well.
Warm the sweetcorn in the same pan or briefly in the microwave.
Build the bowls: rice first, then chipotle beans, sweetcorn, shredded lettuce and avocado. Add a generous dollop of soured cream and a scattering of coriander.

name: Cacio e Pepe
description: Rome's most perfect pasta — just spaghetti, pecorino romano, parmesan and a serious amount of cracked black pepper. The technique is everything: starchy pasta water turns the cheese into a silky, clinging sauce.
kidNote: The pepper is pronounced — reduce to 1 tsp for children and they'll still get the full cheese pull
tip: Never add the cheese over direct heat — it will seize and clump. Always add it off the heat with pasta water, building the sauce from the steam alone.
steps: Cook spaghetti in well-salted boiling water per pack instructions. While it cooks, toast the cracked pepper in a large dry frying pan for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Mix the pecorino and parmesan together. Add 4–5 tbsp of the hot pasta water to the cheese and stir vigorously until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
Reserve a large cup of pasta water before draining. Add the drained spaghetti to the pepper pan over low heat with a large splash of pasta water, tossing constantly.
Remove from heat. Add the cheese paste and toss vigorously — the steam and starchy water will melt the cheese into a silky, glossy sauce. Add more pasta water splash by splash until perfectly coated.
Serve immediately with extra cracked pepper and a dusting of pecorino.

name: Pasta alla Norma
description: Sicily's greatest pasta — rigatoni with sweet-sour tomato sauce, crispy fried aubergine and a shower of salty ricotta salata. Named after Bellini's opera Norma, because it's perfect.
kidNote: Children tend to love the soft fried aubergine in tomato sauce — ricotta salata can be swapped for mild grated mozzarella
tip: The aubergine must be fried properly in oil until golden and collapsed — not steamed or baked. This is what gives alla Norma its characteristic richness.
ingredients: 80g ricotta salata or firm feta, crumbled
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the aubergine in batches for 8–10 minutes until deeply golden and soft. Drain on kitchen paper and season.
In the same pan, reduce oil to 2 tbsp, fry garlic for 1 minute. Add tomatoes, oregano and chilli flakes, season, and simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce is rich and thick.
Cook the rigatoni in well-salted boiling water per pack instructions. Reserve a cup of pasta water.
Add the fried aubergine to the tomato sauce and stir through. Add the drained pasta and toss together, adding pasta water if needed to loosen.
Serve in warm bowls with ricotta salata crumbled generously over the top and a handful of torn basil.

name: Wild Mushroom Tagliatelle
description: Silky tagliatelle wound through a deeply savoury mushroom cream sauce, built with dried porcini for that forest-floor intensity that fresh mushrooms alone can never achieve.
kidNote: A mild, creamy pasta that kids generally adore — use regular chestnut mushrooms throughout for the most accessible version
tip: Don't skip the porcini soaking liquid — strained and added to the sauce, it delivers more concentrated mushroom flavour than any stock.
ingredients: small bunch of flat-leaf parsley, chopped
steps: Soak dried porcini in 150ml boiling water for 15 minutes. Drain, reserving the soaking liquid strained through a sieve. Roughly chop the rehydrated porcini.
Cook pasta per pack instructions. Meanwhile heat butter and oil, fry shallot for 3 minutes until soft, then add garlic for 1 minute.
Add all the fresh mushrooms and chopped porcini. Cook over high heat for 6–8 minutes until golden and any liquid has evaporated.
Add wine and the strained porcini water, boil for 2 minutes. Add cream and simmer for 3 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon. Season well.
Drain pasta, reserving a cup of water. Toss pasta through the sauce, adding pasta water to loosen. Serve scattered with parsley and parmesan.

name: Spaghetti Aglio, Olio e Peperoncino
description: Naples' midnight pasta — spaghetti with slowly golden-fried garlic, fruity olive oil and chilli, emulsified into a light sauce with pasta water. Five ingredients, fifteen minutes, genuinely brilliant.
kidNote: Omit the chilli and reduce garlic to 2 cloves for a gentle, fragrant pasta that children tend to love
tip: Low and slow is the rule for the garlic — the moment it truly colours, remove from the heat. Golden is perfect; brown is bitter.
ingredients: large handful of flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
steps: Cook spaghetti in generously salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a large mug of pasta water before draining.

While the pasta cooks, gently warm the olive oil in a large pan over low-medium heat. Add the sliced garlic and fry very slowly for 4–5 minutes until pale golden and fragrant. Do not rush or brown it.
Add the chilli flakes, fry for 30 seconds. Remove from heat immediately.
Add the drained spaghetti to the pan, return to low heat. Add pasta water splash by splash, tossing constantly for 2 minutes until the oil and water emulsify into a light, glossy sauce.
Remove from heat, toss through most of the parsley and check seasoning. Serve immediately with remaining parsley scattered over.

name: Dan Dan Noodles
description: Sichuan street noodles in a breathtakingly good sauce of sesame paste, peanut butter, chilli oil and soy — numbing, spicy, rich and completely addictive. No meat required.
kidNote: This is properly spicy — make a mild version omitting chilli oil and Sichuan pepper and they will still love the sesame peanut noodles
tip: Toast and grind the Sichuan peppercorns yourself — pre-ground loses the distinctive floral numbing quality that makes dan dan noodles so singular.
ingredients: 350g fresh or dried Chinese wheat noodles
3 tbsp Chinese sesame paste or tahini
2 tbsp chilli oil (plus extra to serve)
1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
steps: Whisk together sesame paste, peanut butter, soy sauce, chilli oil, rice vinegar, sesame oil, Sichuan pepper, garlic, ginger and sugar. Add warm water gradually until the sauce is smooth and pourable.
Cook noodles per pack instructions. In the last minute, add pak choi to the noodle water until just wilted.
Drain noodles and pak choi, rinse briefly under cold water to stop cooking.
Divide the sauce between 4 bowls. Add the noodles on top and toss each bowl to coat the noodles thoroughly.
Top with pak choi, spring onions and an extra drizzle of chilli oil. Serve immediately while warm.

name: Miso Ramen with Crispy Tofu
description: A deeply savoury miso broth loaded with ramen noodles, crispy pan-fried tofu, soft-boiled egg, sweetcorn and spring onions. Restaurant-quality ramen you can actually make at home.
kidNote: Reduce the miso to 2 tbsp and skip the chilli oil for a mild, warming bowl that most children will happily eat
tip: Don't boil the broth after adding miso — it kills the complex fermented flavour. Stir it in at the end, off the boil.
ingredients: 400g firm tofu, pressed and cut into cubes
steps: Soft-boil the eggs: lower into simmering water for exactly 6½ minutes, then plunge into ice-cold water. Peel carefully and halve just before serving.
Press tofu dry between kitchen paper, then fry in vegetable oil in a non-stick pan for 8–10 minutes, turning, until golden and crispy on all sides. Season with a little soy sauce at the end.
Bring stock to a gentle simmer. Whisk in miso paste (do not boil after this point), soy sauce, mirin and sesame oil. Taste and adjust.
Cook noodles per pack instructions. Drain and divide between 4 deep bowls.
Pour over the hot miso broth. Top each bowl with crispy tofu, a soft-boiled egg half, sweetcorn, beansprouts, spring onions, nori and sesame seeds. Drizzle with chilli oil.
